A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe ChartVerse. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable matching despite substantial reformatting and added analyses.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendix D report original ChartVerse training results, chart and STEM benchmark evaluations, and ablation studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds experiments on model bases, teacher scale and models used for RPE computation in Tables 8–10.

M1.justification: The synthesis pipeline and its components remain unchanged. However, Appendix A replaces v1's GSPO with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), while Section 4.1 still specifies GSPO. This contradiction prevents determining whether the training algorithm actually changed.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same source chart corpora, chart reasoning tasks, six chart benchmarks and five STEM benchmarks. The new teacher-generated 100K dataset and model comparisons retain this coverage while changing sample counts or model configurations.

E2.justification: Tables 2, 3, 6 and 7 retain their comparator sets, including ECD, START, Chart-R1, Qwen3-VL, InternVL3.5 and the dataset, QA-generation and selection alternatives. The additional models serve as internal base, teacher and RPE-component ablations.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 revises raw/retained chart counts from 1.2M/900K to 1M/700K. Added experiments use 4B/8B Thinking bases, compare 100K larger-teacher samples with 600K smaller-teacher samples, and evaluate RPE on 10K charts. Existing benchmark metrics and inference settings remain unchanged; reruns of retained experiments are not established.

E4.justification: v2 adds Instruct-versus-Thinking experiments in Appendix D.4, teacher-scale analysis in D.5, and RPE-model comparisons in Appendix E. Tables 8–10 substantially extend investigation of model compatibility, teacher capacity, and reconstruction reliability beyond the retained ablations.

E5.justification: New Table 10 reports RPE means, standard deviations, quartiles and interquartile ranges across a random subset of 10K charts. These describe between-chart variation. Neither version reports repeated-training uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests for benchmark performance.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation scores remain unchanged, but Tables 8–10 add substantive findings. Thinking-base ChartVerse averages are 63.0 at 4B and 65.1 at 8B. The 235B-teacher/100K SFT condition scores 64.1 versus 62.5 for the 30B-teacher/600K condition. New RPE execution-success results include 88.6% versus 63.2% for 2B Thinking versus Instruct. These are added conditions, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations 1–13 retain the same RPE construction, synthesis definitions and failure-rate filtering mathematics. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same RPE-guided synthesis and truth-anchored QA contributions, together with the claim that ChartVerse-8B exceeds its 30B teacher and approaches Qwen3-VL-32B-Thinking. The new analyses do not redefine these central scientific claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explicit limitations concerning RPE computation costs, numerical/logical answer coverage and teacher capacity. New appendix interpretations attribute the narrow Instruct–Thinking gap to extensive SFT, stronger-teacher results to data quality, and the 2B Thinking RPE choice to discrimination and execution reliability. These substantially expand the explanations and qualifications.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 newly documents benchmark decontamination using CLIP similarity above 0.65. The abstract explicitly announces code, weights and dataset release at the existing homepage. Resource estimates change, including RPE from 40M calls/4 days to 32M/3 days, inverse QA from 5M calls/5 days to 4M/4 days, and CoT processing from 7 to 5 days. These are reporting changes; newly performed runs or online availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Sections 1–2 substantially expand citations into retrieval, table QA, GUI reasoning and broader multimodal research while retaining the original positioning narrative. Some placements appear mismatched: STABLE, identified in the bibliography as nearest-neighbor search research, is cited among rule-based chart-rendering approaches.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the six main sections are retained. v2 adds Limitations and Acknowledgments, extends Appendix D, inserts a new Appendix E and relabels the former E as F. Author ordering, affiliations and citation style also change.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column report to a two-column layout, with widespread resizing and relocation of displays. Table 4 is transposed into a source-per-row format, Tables 8–10 are added, and existing prompt tables are renumbered 11–16. The original figures and case-study graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: Tables 8–10, explicit limitations and decontamination disclosure add useful evidence and transparency. However, v2 introduces a GSPO/GRPO contradiction between Section 4.1 and Appendix A, alongside apparently mismatched research citations such as STABLE in Section 2. The teacher-scale experiment also changes sample budget, limiting its causal interpretation. These benefits and new reliability problems leave the net quality direction unclear.
